# Amadu Kamal · Model Analysis Hub

> Amadu Kamal (also known as Amadu Kamal Jnr, Kamal Amadu, and kamaldeenjnr on GitHub) is a Ghanaian data analyst and software engineer, and the founder of Model Analysis Hub. He builds websites, statistical and geospatial models, and dashboards, and created QuantAI, a free in-browser data analysis tool.

Amadu Kamal built his skills through mentors and real projects. He combines the statistics needed to build a model you can trust with the engineering needed to turn it into something people use. He is based in Ghana and works with clients remotely.

- Occupation: Data Analyst, Software Engineer, Founder of Model Analysis Hub

## Expertise

- Statistical and predictive modelling, model validation and risk modelling (R, Python, NumPy, SciPy)
- Geospatial analysis and spatial epidemiology (ArcGIS)
- Websites for organisations, with content systems clients manage themselves
- Dashboards and full-stack web platforms (JavaScript, React, SQL, HTML/CSS)
- Public health data analysis, including malaria risk mapping in Ghana

## Projects

- [Soma](https://modelanalysishub.com/projects.html#soma) (2026, own product): A local food delivery platform for Ho, Hohoe and the Volta Region in Ghana, designed and built by Amadu Kamal. Customer, vendor, rider and admin apps; Mobile Money and card payments through Paystack with automatic payouts; phone notifications; installable web app. Live at https://soma-wmql.onrender.com, source at https://github.com/kamaldeenjnr/soma. Tools: Node.js, Express, SQLite, JavaScript, Paystack, Render.
- [The Sunshine Project website](https://modelanalysishub.com/projects.html#sunshine-project) (2026, client project): A multi-page website for The Sunshine Project, a Ghanaian NGO, designed and built by Amadu Kamal. Includes an admin login so the NGO's team updates programmes, schedules and photos themselves. Live at https://sunshine-project-website.vercel.app. Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, Decap CMS, Vercel.
- [Malaria risk prediction model, Ghana](https://modelanalysishub.com/projects.html#malaria-risk) (2025): A spatial model combining climate and population data to rank Ghana's regions by predicted malaria risk. Tools: Python, R, ArcGIS.
- [Risk modelling: probability of high malaria burden](https://modelanalysishub.com/projects.html#risk-modeling): Estimates the chance that each region's prevalence exceeds 30%, for planning and preparedness.
- [Model validation](https://modelanalysishub.com/projects.html#model-validation): Observed versus predicted prevalence, checking how far the model can be trusted.
- [Healthcare utilisation dashboard](https://modelanalysishub.com/projects.html#healthcare-dashboard): Cost, length of stay, diagnoses and outcomes by region and facility type, with filters.
- [ProjectFlow](https://modelanalysishub.com/projects.html#projectflow) (2025): A full-stack platform for managing university research projects at Undergraduate, Master's and PhD level, from draft to publication. Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SQL.

## QuantAI

- [QuantAI](https://modelanalysishub.com/ai.html): Live and free to use. Everything runs in the browser, so the file is never uploaded and no AI service is involved. Methodology tools: research question builder (PICO/PECO/SPIDER/PCC), rule-based study design advisor, sample size calculator, statistical test selector and reporting checklists (STROBE, CONSORT, STARD, COREQ, PRISMA). Data analysis: reads CSV, TSV and Excel files; Table 1; t-tests, Welch, Mann-Whitney, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, correlation, chi-square, Fisher's exact and McNemar, each chosen by assumption checks (Shapiro-Wilk, Brown-Forsythe, expected counts); linear, logistic, Poisson and modified Poisson regression with diagnostics; Holt-Winters forecasting; APA-style write-ups; and export of every analysis as Stata, Python, R and SPSS code. Results are checked against SciPy and statsmodels.
